title: Veritas Capital - Dedicated capacity discovery
next_steps: Chris to send Dedicated SKU/pricing + burst options (by 2026-03-06)
Maya to share benchmarking checklist and telemetry requirements (by 2026-03-09)
Tom to provide expected QPS and peak concurrency profile (by 2026-03-08)
Schedule follow-up architecture deep-dive with Infra + Security (week of 2026-03-16)
action_items: Chris (AE): Send pricing sheet and example committed capacity bundles - due 2026-03-06
Maya (SE): Share short runbook for Dedicated onboarding + benchmark checklist - due 2026-03-09
Elena (Security): Send SOC2 report request list and KMS/HSM requirements - due 2026-03-08
Marcus (Infra): Provide current GPU estate and firewall/VPC peering constraints - due 2026-03-08
summary: Initial discovery for Dedicated capacity. Customer is evaluating dedicated GPU pools for inference due to data isolation and predictable throughput needs. Key concerns: burst capacity, autoscaling policies, latency SLOs (p95/p99), model quantization and compatibility, and security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Next steps are pricing, benchmarking checklist, and a security deep-dive.
questions: How does Dedicated handle burst beyond reserved GPUs?
What telemetry and tracing hooks are available for token-level cost breakdown?
Can we pin specific model versions and quantization profiles?
What is the onboarding timeline and typical POC duration?
transcript:
[00:00] Chris Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Chris from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We've got Maya our SE and Jordan from CSM on. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Tom Henderson: Good, thanks. Tom here. We've got Priya, Marcus and Elena on our side.
[00:12] Maya Li: Hi team, thanks for the time. Quick agenda - understand current infra & workloads, isolation/compliance needs, expected throughput, and then walk through Dedicated capabilities.
[00:23] Priya Rao: Sounds good. I'll be honest, we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary driver is data isolation and predictable latency for our customer-facing summarization service, also cost predictability.
[00:34] Marcus Lee: From infra perspective, we run a mix of on-prem GPU clusters and cloud VMs. We don't want user data leaving our tenancy.
[00:41] Elena Gomez: Security wise, SOC2 and encryption-at-rest are musts. KMS integration and audit logs are big for us.
[00:48] Chris Patel: Great, makes sense. Can you share rough qps and concurrency? That helps sizing.
[00:54] Tom Henderson: Baseline is ~50 qps with 10 token average responses, peaks up to 250 qps during batch reporting windows, and concurrency spikes to ~40 concurrent requests sometimes. We also expect growth 2x in 6 months.
[01:09] Maya Li: Helpful. So you're seeing steady baseline with periodic spikes. For Dedicated we typically provision reserved GPUs for baseline and allow burst capacity on demand - depending on contract you can get burst to hosted pool or extra reserved burst nodes.
[01:24] Priya Rao: Can you clarify burst? We don't want noisy neighbors impacting latency.
[01:29] Maya Li: Sure. There are a few patterns: 1) Reserved-only: everything stays in your Dedicated pool - predictable performance but higher commit. 2) Reserved with burst to Redwood-hosted spare capacity - bursts are elastically provisioned but go through policy routing and may have slightly higher p99. 3) Hybrid private routing into your VPC on-prem for overflow - more complex but keeps traffic inside your network.
[01:49] Marcus Lee: Option 2 worries me. If burst goes to hosted spare capacity, how is isolation enforced? Are there tenancy boundaries?
[01:56] Maya Li: Isolation is logical. In Option 2, customer data is encrypted in transit and at rest; we can scoping configure network egress controls, but it's not hardware isolated. For full hardware isolation you need dedicated physical pools or on-prem/private deployment.
[02:11] Elena Gomez: For compliance, we need control plane audit logs and key ownership. Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:17] Chris Patel: Yes - Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS with HSM integration and we can surface audit logs. For Dedicated we have options to integrate with your KMS depending on deployment. I'll flag Maya to follow up with specifics.
[02:28] Tom Henderson: What GPUs are we talking about? A100? H100? Pricing differences matter.
[02:33] Maya Li: We support multiple accelerator types. For Dedicated we commonly offer A100 and H100 profiles. H100 helps for large context and throughput but is pricier. We can map model family and sequence length to the recommended GPU.
[02:45] Priya Rao: Speaking of models, we run Llama variants and fine-tuned open models. We use quantization for cost. How does Redwood handle KV cache and quantization compatibility?
[02:55] Maya Li: Our runtime supports quantization paths (4-bit/8-bit) and manages KV cache for autoregressive models. There are per-model compatibility notes - sometimes 4-bit quant leaves minor quality shifts; we'll run evals during POC. We also support pinning model versions so rollouts won't surprise you.
[03:13] Marcus Lee: Latency targets - we need p95 < 120ms for short prompts. Can Dedicated meet that?
[03:18] Maya Li: Depends on model size and batching. For small models on H100 with right batching, p95 targets are achievable. We'll need your prompt length distribution and token counts. Also, we can tune batching windows to reduce cost while keeping p95 under target.
[03:32] Tom Henderson: What about autoscaling? We can't sustain a manager to manually add nodes during spikes.
[03:37] Maya Li: Dedicated autoscaling can be configured by policy - target CPU/GPU utilization or queue depth. There is also a warm pool concept for fast scale-up. Warm nodes bring up faster but are part of commit. Burst to hosted is the fastest but as noted has tradeoffs.
[03:52] Elena Gomez: Auditability - we need per-request logs for the audit trail. Can you redact sensitive fields?
[03:59] Jordan Alvarez: We can emit per-request telemetry and logs to your SIEM via forwarders. Redaction rules can be applied at ingestion. For Private deployments you get more control.
[04:10] Priya Rao: Onboarding timeline - how long to stand up Dedicated and run a meaningful POC?
[04:15] Maya Li: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-6 weeks for reserved pools + testing; POC can be 2-4 weeks depending on benchmark scope. If you have infra ready and share a small workload, we can do an accelerated pilot.
[04:27] Marcus Lee: What's the failure mode if a node goes down during peak? Do you have fallback routing?
[04:32] Maya Li: Yes, Smart routing will fallback to compatible model variants in other zones or to hosted pool if policy allows. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to previous model versions.
[04:42] Tom Henderson: Cost: we need an example of committed bundles and burst pricing. Priya, finance will want a 12-month commitment comparison.
[04:50] Chris Patel: I'll send a pricing sheet with committed monthly GPU equivalents and burst per-minute rates. We can also model sample cost given your token estimates.
[04:59] Priya Rao: For evaluation, we want to run a benchmarking harness - measure throughput, latency p50/p95/p99, and token cost. Can you provide a checklist for telemetry and required artifacts?
[05:09] Maya Li: Yes, I'll share a benchmark checklist - include prompt corpus, 24h traffic slice, target SLAs, and any compliance constraints. We'll also want a couple of representative fine-tuned models.
[05:19] Tom Henderson: Security - Elena will want SOC2, ISO certs and details on SSO/SAML support. Also curious about data residency options.
[05:28] Elena Gomez: Also key rotation policy and whether Redwood stores plaintext keys.
[05:31] Chris Patel: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and RBAC. For keys, we can integrate with customer-managed KMS; Redwood does not store plaintext private keys - standard KMS flows. I'll include the security pack, and we can schedule a security deep-dive.
[05:42] Priya Rao: One more: model rollouts. We need canary testing and ability to rollback quickly if quality regressions occur.
[05:48] Maya Li: We have rollout policies - percentage-based canary, A/B tests, automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. We also capture model metrics so you can compare.
[05:58] Tom Henderson: For the POC, we want to validate both latency and quality. If you can demonstrate consistent p95 and no data leakage that's a win.
[06:07] Chris Patel: Noted. Quick clarification: Do you prefer burst to hosted capacity for cost reasons or would you rather pay more for pure isolation?
[06:14] Priya Rao: For Phase 1 we can accept burst-to-hosted if encryption and logs meet requirements, but long term we'd prefer hardware isolation once volume justifies it.
[06:24] Marcus Lee: Agreed. Also need to confirm network egress and VPC peering - we can't open wide egress.
[06:31] Maya Li: We can do VPC peering and private network connectivity for Dedicated, and for Private deployments we can run the control plane in your VPC. We'll document required firewall rules in the onboarding pack.
[06:43] Elena Gomez: Let's talk SLA - uptime and latency SLOs, and penalties? Is that in enterprise contract?
[06:49] Chris Patel: Yes SLAs are part of Dedicated enterprise contracts. We'll include typical uptime SLAs and latency objectives; specifics vary by commitment level.
[06:58] Priya Rao: Any reference customers in finance? We need examples of banks using Dedicated for PII-sensitive workloads.
[07:05] Chris Patel: I can share anonymized references; we have customers in fintech and regulated sectors. I'll include that in the follow-up.
[07:12] Tom Henderson: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[07:15] Chris Patel: Recap: Chris will send pricing and reference customers; Maya sends benchmark checklist and onboarding runbook; Elena will send SOC2/controls questions; Marcus will provide infra details and current GPU estate; Tom will share traffic profiles and target SLAs. We'll schedule a security deep dive the week of March 16. Does that capture it?
[07:35] Priya Rao: Yes.
[07:36] Elena Gomez: Yep.
[07:37] Jordan Alvarez: I'll create a shared folder for artifacts and track action items.
[07:41] Chris Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email.
[07:44] Tom Henderson: Thanks all.
[07:46] [meeting ends]
